day: Our Lady of Sorrows on Tuesday of week 24 in Ordinary Time
text:
There is something tender in how Jesus, even in his suffering, makes sure his mother is held. From the cross, he gives her a son. He gives the beloved disciple a mother. What might have looked like loss—a son dying—becomes instead a new belonging. Mary does not stand alone.

Paul writes to us the same truth in different words: we are one body, many parts. Not every part does the same work. Not every gift looks the same. But we need each other. We belong to each other. In that belonging, we are whole. The beloved disciple took Mary into his home, not as a duty but as a gift—and in receiving her, he received something essential.

On this day when we honor Mary's sorrow, we might notice that even her deepest pain becomes a doorway to deeper communion. She does not carry her grief alone. And we, scattered as we are in our different callings and gifts, are held together by something stronger than our isolation. We are his people. We are each other's home.

If you find yourself alone with something hard to carry today, you might sit with the image of Jesus making sure his mother is not left without family—and ask where your own family in Christ might be waiting to walk with you.
